identity.mechanic: The Lamp. Every player has a Lamp; it only matters once Moths care about it.

keywords.name: Heat
keywords.text: each spell you cast adds 1 Heat as it is cast. Heat goes back to 0 at the very start of your turn, before any Start of Turn effects, so the Heat you end the turn on is the Heat you fight with.

keywords.name: Flare
keywords.text: when your Heat goes above your Flashpoint, the Lamp Flares: Heat drops to 0 (the excess is lost) and every **Flare:** effect triggers. A Flare can happen while recruiting or in a fight.

identity.plays: Each Recruit Phase is a small brew. You build Heat by casting spells and Stoking, and you decide where to stop. Stay at or under the Flashpoint and your End of Turn effects pay out by how hot the Lamp is, best at exactly the Flashpoint. Go over and you lose that Heat, but every Flare effect fires, and a Flare build wants to go over as often as it can. Heat you end on carries into the fight, where hawk-moths and omen-readers Stoke it further, so a Lamp left at 7 can Flare in the middle of a fight. The tribe's choices are about order: which spell first, which unit sits next to which, and when to sell the Moth that stops your Lamp from Flaring.

units.name: Six-spot Burnet
units.text: Has Bristle 1, plus 1 for every 2 Heat you have.

units.name: The Uncertain
units.text: Start of Turn: add an Uncertain Phial to your hand.

units.name: Treacle Painter
units.text: End of Turn: give another random Moth +1/+1 permanently for every 2 Heat you have.

units.name: Lamp-Fanner
units.text: After you cast a spell: Stoke 1.

units.name: Skep Pilferer
units.text: Once a turn, after you cast a spell: gain 1 gold.

units.name: The Old Lady
units.text: Once a turn, when your Lamp would Flare while recruiting, it doesn't: your Heat stays at your Flashpoint. (Fights can still Flare.)

units.name: Show-Globe Keeper
units.text: Twice a turn, when you sell a unit: add a Phial to your hand.

units.name: Pestle Noctuid
units.text: After you cast a spell on a unit next to this: give +1/+1 permanently to a random unit next to this that wasn't the target.

units.name: Eyed Hawk-moth
units.text: Whenever this is attacked: the attacker loses Attack equal to half your Heat (this fight), then Stoke 1.
units.golden: The attacker loses Attack equal to your Heat, then Stoke 2.

units.name: Burnt-Ring Senior
units.text: Flare: give your other Moths +1/+1 permanently.

units.name: The Spectacle
units.text: End of Turn: give your other Moths +1/+1 permanently, or +2/+2 if your Heat is exactly your Flashpoint.

units.name: The Herald
units.text: Start of Turn: Stoke 3. When you Tier up: Stoke 2.
units.golden: Stoke 6. When you Tier up: Stoke 4.

units.name: Burnished Brass
units.text: Your Phials, Uncertain ones too, are cast twice on the same target. Each cast counts as a spell.

units.name: Lamplit Compounder
units.text: After you cast a spell on a Moth: it also gains +1/+1 permanently for each Heat you have.

units.name: Mother Shipton
units.text: Start of Combat: deal twice your Heat in damage to the enemy across and each enemy beside it. Whenever another friendly Moth dies: Stoke 1.

units.name: Atropos
units.text: Counts as every tribe. Once a turn, when your Lamp Flares while recruiting: take a random unit from your shop into your hand (it is Created).

units.name: Dame Pavonia
units.text: Can't gain stats. Your other Moths' End of Turn effects trigger twice.

units.name: The Alchymist
units.text: Your Flashpoint is 3 instead of 7. After your Lamp Flares: Stoke 1.

units.name: Old Carbonaria
units.text: End of Turn: give your Moths +1/+1 permanently for every 2 Heat you gained this turn, counting Heat lost to Flares.

extras.name: Phial
extras.text: (spell, Created, costs 0): *Give a unit +1/+1.* (It scales like any spell.)

extras.name: Uncertain Phial
extras.text: (spell, Created, costs 0): *Give a unit +1/+1, then Stoke 0, 1 or 2 at random.* (It scales like any spell, and counts as a Phial.)

builds.name: Simmer at Seven
builds.text: The Old Lady, The Spectacle, Treacle Painter, Lamplit Compounder, Dame Pavonia. You count to exactly 7 every turn. The Herald and Lamp-Fanner get you close, the last Phial tips you over, and The Old Lady catches it. The Compounder makes each later spell worth more than the one before, so the order of casts is the puzzle: cheap Phials first to raise Heat, then the best spell on the Compounder's favourite target. Pavonia doubles The Spectacle and the Painter at the end. Spike's build: little luck once the pieces are in.

builds.name: Boil Over
builds.text: Lamp-Fanner, The Herald, Burnished Brass, Burnt-Ring Senior, Atropos, The Alchymist. You want as many Flares as possible. Brass makes each Phial two casts, each worth 2 Heat with the Fanner, so one Phial is 4 Heat. Each Flare buffs the board through the Senior, and the first one each turn steals a shop unit through Atropos. With The Alchymist at Flashpoint 3, a Flare takes 3 more Heat after her Stoke. Sell The Old Lady when you switch to this; she stops Flares.

builds.name: Lamp in the Fight
builds.text: Six-spot Burnet and Eyed Hawk-moth in front, Mother Shipton behind, Burnt-Ring Senior anywhere. End the turn at 7 (Simmer pieces help) so Shipton's Start of Combat hits three enemies for 14. Then every hit on the Hawk-moth and every Moth death Stokes, and the next point of Heat Flares mid-fight: the Senior's permanent buff lands during the fight and the Burnet's Bristle climbs again as Heat rebuilds. The Old Lady only catches Flares while recruiting, so she can sit in this build. Mind the trade: a mid-fight Flare drops Heat to 0, which shrinks the Burnet's Bristle and the Hawk-moth's drain until Heat builds again.

builds.name: Quick Flashpoint (a crossover of the two)
builds.text: The Alchymist plus The Spectacle: at Flashpoint 3, "exactly your Flashpoint" is easy, so The Spectacle pays its top rate every turn. Flare on purpose mid-turn, rebuild to exactly 3 before End of Turn, and you get both. Old Carbonaria fits every build, because she counts all Heat gained, flared or not.

builds.name: In a lobby: Fairies
builds.text: Phials are aimed spells, the only thing that buffs a Shy unit. Every Phial on a Shy unit is 2 gold next turn, and Show-Globe Keeper turns selling into more Phials. Rings stack on top of spell buffs.

builds.name: In a lobby: Birds
builds.text: a Bird Flying South is still a sale, so Show-Globe Keeper makes a Phial from it, and it comes home doubled, Phial buffs included.

builds.name: In a lobby: Oozes
builds.text: an Ooze Eating a Moth while recruiting is a death, so Mother Shipton Stokes. Eat a cheap Moth to tip the Lamp over its Flashpoint.

builds.name: In a lobby: Hedgerow folk
builds.text: Pass X to the rightmost unit; put the Pestle Noctuid's neighbours there and spells splash along the row.

builds.name: In a lobby: Any tribe
builds.text: Atropos counts as every tribe, so every other tribe's "your Birds / your Oozes" buff hits her, and a stolen shop unit is Created, worth 0 to sell but a Phial to Show-Globe Keeper. Harvest Supper and the neutral spell-help units add Heat like any spell.

risks: **Rules load.** Heat, Stoke, Flashpoint, Flare, plus "Heat gained" for one card. The Lamp needs a clear on-screen dial with the Flashpoint marked, and a preview of the Heat each spell would bring when you hover it, or the exact-7 game becomes a mental-arithmetic chore.

**Spell supply is unknown.** Shop spell prices aren't set. If spells are dear, the tribe lives on Phials alone and The Uncertain and Show-Globe Keeper become must-buys. If they're cheap, Skep Pilferer and the Compounder may be too good.
**Hand clog.** Four hand slots and Phials every turn. That is a real choice, but it can push out bought units.

**Pavonia with Carbonaria** doubles Carbonaria's board-wide payout: in a Flare-heavy turn, roughly 150–190 stats. That is above the Tier 6 top end. It needs two Tier 6s from different builds, so I've left it as the high roll, but it's the first number to check.
**Fairies economy.** Free Phials on Shy units could print gold. Watch for a Moth-Fairy pair beating both tribes alone.
**Async fights** must record each board's end-of-turn Heat and Flashpoint, and replay in-fight Flares the same way every time.
**In-fight Flares are hard to read.** They need a Lamp flash and a visible buff, or the fight looks random.
**The Old Lady fights the Flare build.** That's intended (it's a sell decision), but a player who finds her early may stay on Simmer by default.
**Thin early game.** Before Tier 3 there's little Heat to pay out. Burnet and The Uncertain carry turns 1–4 on their bodies.

**Loop check done:** no card makes a spell on a Flare. An earlier "Flare: add a Phial" on The Alchymist looped with Lamp-Fanner and Burnished Brass, so I cut it. Heat sources are fixed per turn (spells, The Herald, the Fanner per cast) or per event in a fight (hits, deaths, Flares), and none feeds another.
**The Uncertain Phial is the tribe's one dice roll.** Cast early it is safe, since later casts can correct the count; cast last it is a gamble on the exact 7, which The Old Lady can catch.

tier_check.note: Tier 1 (body 4): Burnet 2/2 and Uncertain 1/3 fit. The Uncertain gives about +2 stats and 1 to 3 Heat a turn (2 on average) (≈0.5 body, target 0.4). The Burnet's Bristle reaches 4 late, slightly above the in-fight 0.6 body; on purpose, so the tribe's Tier 1 stays a home for front-row Heat play.
Tier 2 (body 6): Treacle Painter gives 4–6 a turn (0.7–1 body, top of range). Skep Pilferer gives 1 gold a turn, the usual Tier 2 economy. Lamp-Fanner is a pure enabler: no stats, it doubles Heat.
Tier 3 (body 7): Pestle Noctuid gives 6–8 a turn (≈1 body, a little over 0.8). Eyed Hawk-moth removes 6–9 Attack a fight and Stokes (within 0.7–1.4). The Old Lady and Show-Globe Keeper are enablers.

Tier 4 (body 8.5): Burnt-Ring Senior gives 10–20 (1.2–2.3 bodies) and The Spectacle 10, or 20 at exactly the Flashpoint; target 1.3. The top rates are above on purpose: they reward hitting the mark or Flaring twice. The Herald is an enabler, Burnished Brass the multiplier.

Tier 5 (body 12): Compounder gives about 20 a turn at four casts and up to about 44 with The Herald (target 24, top 60). Mother Shipton deals 42 at Heat 7 against an in-fight target of 48, before her Stokes. Atropos gives about one free unit a turn plus every tribe's buffs: strong Tier 5 economy.

Tier 6 (body 14): Carbonaria gives 36 (Simmer) to about 96 (Flare) a turn, around the 56 target and inside the top 140. Pavonia and The Alchymist are multipliers. Each roughly doubles one build's payout. Pavonia gives up her own growth to do it: a deliberate drawback that makes her a spell sink, still triggering every cast effect.

rationale: I borrowed the Quacks pot because it is already an apothecary's brew and its "past 7 it blows" is the seed's "drawn to the flame knowing the danger".
I dropped the random bag draw. Bramble has no turn timer, and Johnny and Spike both want to plan, so the luck stays in the shop rolls.
Overshooting resets Heat instead of carrying a separate penalty: the loss is built in, as in Quacks, with no extra rule.
I made overshooting a trigger too (Flare:), so one dial gives two opposite builds rather than one build and a failure state.
Heat resets each turn, which caps every per-turn payoff at the Flashpoint: the tribe's runaway brake.
Heat carries into the fight, which links the recruit puzzle to combat without a second resource.
I named the Flashpoint as a number cards can move (Alchymist) and read (Spectacle, Old Lady); the main lever for cards that overlap.
One token, the Phial, keeps spell supply in the tribe's hands and feeds every cast trigger, including other tribes' Shy units.
Quacks' flask, which puts back an exploding chip, became The Old Lady: a safety valve for Simmer and a sell decision for Boil Over.
I put the seed's "spells get stronger the more you cast" literally at Tier 5 (Compounder), because pricing by Heat makes it compound.
I cut every "Flare: make a spell" text after the loop check.
Names came last, each from the real moth or seed figure whose habit matched the text: the Old Lady snuffs, the Spectacle measures, the Herald starts the season, Atropos steals in disguise.

changes.what: Heat keyword now says the reset comes before any Start of Turn effects.
changes.why: Without the order, The Herald's Start of Turn Stoke could be wiped at once.

changes.what: Makes an Uncertain Phial, which Stokes 0, 1 or 2 at random, instead of a plain Phial.
changes.why: An apprentice unsure of the dose; makes the early count to 7 a live push-your-luck call.

changes.what: New token: Uncertain Phial, +1/+1 then Stoke 0, 1 or 2 at random.
Only stops Flares while recruiting; fights can still Flare.
changes.why: Her limit didn't say if it covered fights; recruit-only keeps her the Simmer valve and fits Lamp in the Fight.

changes.what: Names the buffed unit: a random neighbour that wasn't the spell's target.
changes.why: "Another" could mean other than the target or other than the Noctuid.

changes.what: Drains the attacker first, then Stokes.
changes.why: Stoking first at Heat 7 Flared, dropped Heat to 0, and drained nothing.

changes.what: Also Stokes 2 when you Tier up.
changes.why: Gives the Herald, who announces each season, a moment of its own beyond a flat battery.

changes.what: Says the repeat casts hit the same target, each counts as a spell, and Uncertain Phials count.
changes.why: The target decided how Pestle Noctuid and Lamplit Compounder pay out.
